meta.protocol: one identification per window at zero command (the probe bank sees only the static device aberration); the coefficients are frozen for all test phases, so every windowed_fit frame is a single open-loop prediction

device.description: Sim2f with static SLM aberration and roughness

model.description: ideal Sim2f, same geometry, no errors

oracle.description: least-squares projection of the device panel phase onto the model's Noll 2..11 basis; a labelled upper bound, not a result

confirmation.description: one held-out shot, drawn from its own RNG stream and checked to match no scored case; the fit is kept only if its window-frame relative L1 on that shot is at most CONFIRM_RATIO times the uncorrected model's on the same shot
confirmation.rationale: a ratio, not an absolute level, so the gate needs no calibrated constant and no oracle: it only asks whether the fitted model explains a shot it was not fitted on better than no correction

findings: The requested 'tiny spot, D86 < 8 px' is below this geometry's diffraction floor of 14.21 px (grid=128, ccd=256), so the tiny group uses the floor itself: the spot is still ~7x smaller than the 96 px window.
l1_out divides by the truth energy outside the window; when the window captures ~all light (tiny group) that denominator is under 1% and l1_out is unstable -- read l1_all and ee_out_err there.
Noll 14 (0.18 rad) and the 0.06 rad roughness are outside the fitted basis; the oracle projection leaves 0.082 rad RMS unmodelled, so even the oracle is an upper bound for this model class.
The device has no detector noise (exposure_ms=0), so the fit is an optimistic bound on what a real camera would allow.

The fit is identified once per window at zero command and frozen. Re-identifying per phase was rejected: the free basis (Noll 4..11) overlaps the commanded test phases, so one window shot cannot separate commanded from static aberration and the fit absorbs the command, over-correcting a phase it already knows.

Identification, not extrapolation, is the bottleneck. The 64x64@128,108 window reaches a fit residual of 0.0059 and a coefficient RMSE of 0.046 rad against the oracle, while 96x96@128,108 stops at 0.241 rad with a projection ratio of -1.03: a sign-flipped, over-scaled copy of the same phase. Negating a pupil phase conjugates the field, which point-mirrors the far field, so on the centred, nearly symmetric identification shot the branches are hard to tell apart -- and the fit's eight free modes also absorb part of the out-of-basis residual (Noll 14 + roughness). The consequence is that the frame prefers whichever branch the fit chose: on that same shot the fit scores 0.0083 window L1 while its opposite branch scores 0.0400 and zero aberration 0.0517. A low residual on the identification shot therefore certifies nothing about the branch.

FitResult.ok is not a trust gate: it reports rank and finiteness, not whether the coefficients are the device's. The confirmation gate is the deployable test; at ratio 1 it keeps the 64x64@128,108 fit (confirm_l1 0.0399 vs nominal 0.1536, oracle floor 0.0110) and rejects 96x96@128,108 (ratio 1.75 vs 1).
The gate does catch the sign-flipped 96x96@128,108 fit on this shot, so it is worth more than FitResult.ok -- but it only bounds the window error and cannot certify the far field.

The probe shot is always well lit: at zero command the windows capture 0.938 to 1.000 of the light, so a failed identification here is not a starved probe but the gauge degeneracy above. A per-phase probe would be starved instead -- the commanded defocus throws the light out of the window -- which is why identification is done once at zero command.

Before the gate decides anything, the fitted amplitude is biased, and the bias costs the outside-window energy: on the random group the raw 64x64@128,108 fit cuts l1_all 0.104 -> 0.039 but moves ee_out_err 0.0015 -> 0.0055, while the oracle at the true amplitude holds it at 0.0011. The over-scale is what the frame objective trades for the unmodelled Noll 14 and roughness spread, so the window-only fit buys in-window fidelity at some cost in far-field energy.
